note: NKX6-2 disorder exhibits a broad spectrum from milder spastic ataxia to severe hypomyelination with global delay; however, epilepsy has been reported even in the absence of overt hypomyelination.

evidence.text: The study shows a phenotypic spectrum with neonatal onset, global psychomotor delay, and worse prognosis at the severe end, and childhood onset with mainly motor signs at the milder end, but explicitly notes phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination and diffuse hypomyelination without seizures.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: The phenotypic and neuroimaging expression in NKX6-2 is described and it is shown that phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination and diffuse hypomyelination without seizures can occur.

evidence.text: Biallelic NKX6-2 mutations were identified in individuals displaying childhood-onset spastic-ataxia phenotypes with slow progression, while earlier-onset disease presentation was associated with prominent brain hypomyelination.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 cause progressive spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: Affected members of two families had childhood onset disease with very slow progression. They are still alive in their 30s and 40s and show predominant ataxia and cerebellar atrophy features on imaging. Affected members of the third family had a similar but earlier-onset presentation associated with brain hypomyelination.
